outputs.L1: An object of the present invention is to provide an organic EL module that includes an organic EL element having an electrode configuration that provides both a light-emitting function and a hovering-detection function. The organic EL module has a specific control-circuit configuration, can be produced in a compact, miniaturized form, and enables process simplification. The present invention also provides a smart device and an illuminating device incorporating the organic EL module. The organic EL module includes an electrostatic-capacitance-type hovering-detection circuit unit having a hovering-detection function, and a light-emitting-element driving circuit unit configured to drive an organic EL panel. The organic EL panel includes a pair of planar electrodes disposed opposite each other therein. The pair of electrodes is connected to the light-emitting-element driving circuit unit, either one of the pair of electrodes serves as a hovering-detection electrode, and the hovering-detection electrode is connected to the hovering-detection circuit unit.

The present invention aims to provide an organic EL module containing an organic EL element with an electrode structure that performs both light emission and hovering detection. The module has a particular control-circuit arrangement that enables a compact, miniaturized design and simplifies manufacturing processes. The invention also provides smart devices and lighting devices incorporating this organic EL module.

The organic EL module includes a capacitive hovering-detection circuit unit for detecting hovering objects and a light-emitting-element drive circuit unit that operates an organic EL panel. The panel has two planar electrodes positioned opposite each other internally. Both electrodes are connected to the light-emitting-element drive circuit unit, while either one serves as a hovering-detection electrode and is additionally connected to the hovering-detection circuit unit.
outputs.L3:
The invention provides an organic electroluminescent (EL) module that combines a light-emitting function with a hovering-detection function. Its control circuit is specifically configured to facilitate miniaturization of the module while simplifying the manufacturing process.

The module includes an electrostatic-capacitance hovering-detection circuit and a light-emitting-element driving circuit for driving an organic EL panel. The organic EL panel has a pair of planar electrodes arranged opposite each other within the panel. Both electrodes are electrically connected to the light-emitting-element driving circuit and cooperate to operate the panel’s light-emitting elements.

In addition, one of the planar electrodes is shared between the two functions. Besides serving as an electrode for light emission, it also functions as a hovering-detection electrode and is connected to the electrostatic-capacitance hovering-detection circuit. This shared-electrode arrangement reduces the number of separate components and electrical connections required, thereby supporting a smaller module design and a more straightforward manufacturing process.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to an organic electroluminescent (EL) module, a smart device incorporating the module, and a lighting device capable of both emitting light and detecting the approach or hovering of an object. The organic EL module includes an organic EL panel having a pair of substantially planar electrodes arranged to face each other, with an organic light-emitting layer disposed between the electrodes. A light-emission driving circuit applies a driving voltage between the electrodes to cause the organic light-emitting layer to emit light.

The module further includes a capacitance detection circuit configured to detect a change in capacitance caused by a finger, hand, stylus, or other conductive object approaching the organic EL panel. At least one of the planar electrodes of the organic EL panel functions not only as an electrode for driving the light-emitting layer but also as a detection electrode for capacitive hovering detection. The detection circuit monitors an electrical characteristic associated with this shared electrode and determines whether an object is present near the panel based on a detected capacitance change. Thus, proximity or hovering input can be detected without requiring a separate touch-sensor electrode to be formed over or adjacent to the light-emitting surface.

The light-emission driving circuit and the capacitance detection circuit may be selectively connected to the shared electrode by a switching circuit. Light emission and capacitance detection may be performed during different time periods so that the electrical signal used to drive the organic EL panel does not substantially interfere with the detection signal. For example, the panel may be driven to emit light during a light-emission period, while capacitance is measured during a detection period in which the light-emission drive signal is temporarily interrupted or controlled. Because these periods can be switched at high speed, the panel appears to emit light continuously while also providing responsive hovering detection.

A controller may coordinate the light-emission driving circuit, the capacitance detection circuit, and the switching circuit. Based on the detected capacitance, the controller may determine the presence, position, movement, or distance of an approaching object and may change the display or illumination state accordingly. The controller may, for example, turn the panel on or off, adjust its brightness, select a displayed function, or initiate an operation of a device before the user physically touches the panel.

Since an existing electrode of the organic EL panel is used for both light emission and capacitive detection, an additional sensor panel or separately patterned detection-electrode layer is unnecessary. This shared-electrode configuration reduces the number of components and electrical connections, decreases the thickness and installation area of the module, and simplifies alignment and assembly. It can also reduce manufacturing complexity and cost while preserving a broad, substantially uniform light-emitting surface.

The organic EL module may be incorporated into various smart devices, including mobile terminals, wearable devices, household appliances, control panels, switches, information terminals, and human-machine interfaces. In such applications, the light-emitting surface can provide visual information or guidance while simultaneously serving as a non-contact input region. The module may also be incorporated into a lighting device so that illumination can be controlled in response to the approach or motion of a user.

Accordingly, the invention provides a compact multifunctional structure in which a single organic EL panel performs both optical-output and proximity-sensing functions. By sharing at least one planar electrode between the light-emission system and the capacitive hovering-detection system, the invention enables miniaturization, reduces component count, and facilitates efficient manufacture of smart devices and lighting devices with intuitive non-contact operation.

### An Object of Wonder

On the highest shelf of the old library stood an object of uncertain origin. It was small, round, and made of a metal that seemed to change color with the light. No one knew who had placed it there or what purpose it served.

To the librarian, it was an object of curiosity. To visiting scholars, it became an object of study. Children saw it as an object of wonder, imagining that it might be a key to another world.

Perhaps the object itself was unimportant. What mattered was the attention it inspired. It reminded everyone that even the simplest thing can become meaningful when viewed with curiosity, imagination, and hope.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing an organic electroluminescent module that combines light emission with capacitive hovering detection, including its circuit and electrode configuration.
counterfactuals.output: An organic electroluminescent module includes a substrate, an organic electroluminescent device disposed in a display region of the substrate, and a capacitive detection circuit configured to detect a conductive object spaced from the module. The organic electroluminescent device includes a first electrode, an organic light-emitting layer, and a second electrode arranged in a stacked configuration. At least one of the first electrode and the second electrode is segmented into a plurality of electrode portions selectively operable as light-emission electrodes and capacitive sensing electrodes. A drive circuit supplies emission signals to selected electrode portions during an emission period, and a sensing circuit supplies a detection signal to, or receives a detection signal from, the electrode portions during a sensing period different from the emission period. The sensing circuit determines hovering of the conductive object based on a change in capacitance between the sensing electrodes and the object. A switching circuit selectively couples the segmented electrode portions to the drive circuit or the sensing circuit, while one or more adjacent electrodes are maintained at a reference potential or driven with a guard signal to reduce interference from the light-emission drive. The module thereby provides organic electroluminescent display operation and non-contact hovering detection using a shared electrode structure with reduced thickness and component count.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize an invention for a miniaturized organic EL panel in which one of two opposing planar electrodes also functions as a hover-detection electrode.
counterfactuals.output: The invention is a miniaturized organic electroluminescent (EL) panel having an organic light-emitting layer between two opposing planar electrodes. One of these electrodes serves both as an EL drive electrode and as a capacitive sensing electrode for detecting a finger or other object hovering near the panel. By sharing the electrode instead of adding a separate hover sensor, the design reduces component count, thickness, wiring, and required mounting area while preserving display and non-contact input functions. Drive and sensing operations may be separated in time or electrically isolated to prevent interference.

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain, using formal patent language, how an organic EL module can integrate a hovering detection circuit with the panel’s existing electrode structure to reduce size and simplify manufacturing.
counterfactuals.output:
An organic electroluminescent module may comprise an organic electroluminescent panel including a first electrode, a second electrode, and an organic light-emitting layer interposed therebetween, and a hovering detection circuit electrically coupled to at least one electrode already provided in the panel. The hovering detection circuit may be configured to detect a variation in capacitance produced when a conductive object, such as a user’s finger or a stylus, approaches the display surface without contacting the display surface.

In one embodiment, at least a portion of the first electrode, the second electrode, a touch-detection electrode, a common electrode, or an auxiliary wiring electrode is selectively used as a hovering-detection electrode. A switching circuit may selectively connect the shared electrode to a display-driving circuit during a display-driving period and to the hovering detection circuit during a hovering-detection period. The display-driving operation and the hovering-detection operation may thereby be performed in a time-division manner. The hovering detection circuit may apply a detection signal to the shared electrode and determine the presence, position, or approach distance of the conductive object based on a change in electrode capacitance, charging time, oscillation frequency, current, or voltage.

Accordingly, a separately formed hovering-detection electrode layer and associated external interconnection substrate may be omitted. Because the hovering-detection function is implemented using an electrode and wiring structure already incorporated into the organic electroluminescent panel, the module thickness, bezel area, component count, and mounting area can be reduced. Further, formation of an additional sensor film, alignment of the sensor film with the panel, and provision of a separate bonding process may be avoided, thereby simplifying manufacturing, improving positional accuracy, and reducing manufacturing cost. Shielding, compensation, and signal-processing circuitry may additionally be provided to suppress interference caused by display-driving signals and to distinguish a hovering-induced capacitance variation from parasitic capacitance and environmental noise.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
